mapName: A Learnable Russia - No Car Metas - 3

metas.name: Bashkir bilingual signs
metas.note: Bashkir bilingual signs are found in Bashkortostan and use “урамы” for street, the same as Tatar, but are often not abbreviated.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Chuvash bilingual signs
metas.note: Chuvash bilingual signs, found in Chuvashia, use “урамӗ” for street.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Cobblestone pavement
metas.note: Cobblestone pavement is notably common in Kaliningrad, Nizhny Tagil in Sverdlovsk, and Kizel in Perm Krai.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: East of Birobidzhan
metas.note: On the east side of the Jewish Autonomous Oblast, the coverage turns from rainy to wet after the rain.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Extended insulator bars
metas.note: Extended insulator bars on poles are notably found in southern Chelyabinsk Oblast and eastern Orenburg Oblast, as well as southern Kemerovo Oblast. Edit from Vincent: Can also be found in Petrozavodsk.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Khabarovsk-Vanino road
metas.note: The Khabarovsk-Vanino road has a mountainous landscape with very sunny coverage. It also drives west with a black car with a blurred, long antenna, which helps to confirm.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Komi bilingual signs
metas.note: Komi bilingual signs, found in the Komi Republic, use “улича” for street.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Mari bilingual signs
metas.note: Mari bilingual signs, found in Mari El, use “урем” for street.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Mari El historical buildings
metas.note: Historical buildings in Mari El often have a unique architecture style. You will frequently see design patterns that include green roofs, red brick sprinkled with white stone details. Local churches commonly feature a similar style.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Mesh framework utility poles
metas.note: Utility poles with a mesh framework are usually found in Petrozavodsk, but can much less commonly be found in cities like Tolyatti.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Poorly-tracked dirt roads
metas.note: In the desert-like region west of the Caspian Sea, this completely flat and rural Generation 4 coverage on small poorly-tracked dirt roads can only be found in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan Oblast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Road to Yakutsk
metas.note: A presence of Siberian larches and large mountains on a mostly paved, but sometimes wide-gravel road indicates the main road south of Yakutsk, with Generation 4 white car appearing north of Berkakit.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Rounded rectangular fences
metas.note: Rounded rectangular fences with a line through the middle are unique to Chelyabinsk Oblast and eastern Orenburg Oblast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Sunset coverage
metas.note: Sunset coverage, with the sun very close to the horizon, with an eastern-looking landscape will be the P-297 in Amur Oblast, roughly between the towns of Never and Sivaki.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Tatar bilingual signs
metas.note: Tatar bilingual signs use “урамы” (ур., abbreviated) for street instead of “улица” and are unsurprisingly found in Tatarstan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Tropical plants
metas.note: Tropical plants in Russia such as palm trees are only found on the Black Sea, most commonly around Sochi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Tunkinsky National Park
metas.note: Tunkinsky National Park in western Buryatia is a very green river basin with tall, jagged mountains to the north. In comparison to most of Buryatia, it is much greener.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Unique bollard
metas.note: This unique bollard, with a grey rectangle and double red reflectors, is specific to the P100 in Kostroma Oblast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: West of Birobidzhan
metas.note: The Jewish Autonomous Oblast effectively has one road of coverage, outside of Birobidzhan. The west side has highly rainy and foggy coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Yellow bands
metas.note: On the main road of Murmansk in generation 4, as well as some roads in Karelia covered in 2018, the vast majority of signposts will have two yellow bands wrapped around them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Yellow pole plates
metas.note: Yellow pole plates attached by a metal band are commonly found in Tatarstan. They are found on the majority of poles, but not all.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.
